The horizontal component of a force is found with the cosine of its angle, because a vector “directed at an angle θ above the horizontal” resolves into \(F\cos\theta\) horizontally and \(F\sin\theta\) vertically [1]. Using the given values, the correct component is  

\[
F_{x}=30\;\text{N}\times\cos30^{\circ}=30\times0.866\approx26\;\text{N}.
\]

A result of 15 N would come from using the sine function (\(30\sin30^{\circ}=15\) N), which is the common error noted in the same passage [1].
